title: Camps C17 — money through the shared helper
subtitle: Rule v1.026 (one money helper) and v1.101 (a minus amount is written “−$50”, real minus sign before the dollar sign). Camps’ text.js stops borrowing Color Belt’s dollars and uses the shared formatMoney (src/lib/money.js); Camps gets its own markedPaidToast. Only one thing on screen changes: a reversed payment in Camper detail’s Payments, “$-335 card (reversed)” → “−$335 card (reversed)”. Everything else Camps shows (“$1,355” to collect, “$350 due”, “Owes $15”, prices, totals, toasts, Compare, Print, Delete camp’s payments total) is spelled the same by both helpers. Amber = what changes.

items.caption: PC 1280×800. Leo Kim’s Camper detail after an admin’s Undo payment: the reversal reads “$-335” (Color Belt’s helper puts the hyphen after the $).
PC. “−$335 card (reversed)”: a real minus sign (−, U+2212) before the $, as Black Belt’s receipt and Finance’s report already write it. The line below and the “$350 due” tag don’t change.
Phone. Same; the line wraps the same way.

footer: Every difference between the two helpers (read side by side: Color Belt’s dollars, screens/testing/text.js:341, vs formatMoney, src/lib/money.js): (1) minus amounts — “$-335” → “−$335”: the only one Camps can show, and only on a reversal (the preview and the database store a reversal as minus cents; every other Camps amount is 0 or more: to collect uses max(0, owes), “Paid $75 more than the total” passes a plus amount). (2) thousands commas — the same: both write “$1,355”, “$10,000”. (3) zero — the same: “$0”. (4) cents — the same for whole cents (“$290.50”); Camps can’t have cents anyway (whole dollars only: price fields and Edit payment refuse cents). (5) not a whole number of cents (e.g. 29050.5) — dollars rounds it, formatMoney shows nothing; can’t happen (the database stores whole cents). (6) not a number (null, text) — both show nothing. (7) minus zero — dollars could write “$-0”, formatMoney “$0”; can’t happen. Not switched in this round: formatDollars on the public family pages (src/register/, the camp form), as the brief says. Data: the preview’s Leo Kim (paid $335 by card), Undo payment pressed to make the reversal (the brief’s example said “cash”; the preview’s camper pays by card — same amount, same change). Drawn: nothing by hand — the After line is the real page with the one amount re-written by the real formatMoney, imported from the running app. Script: mock-c17-money.js.
